risk_register.description: High-resolution PlanetScope imagery, valuable for small horticultural plots, may not be secured due to cost/access constraints, weakening coverage where the sub-pixel problem bites hardest.
risk_register.mitigation: Treat PlanetScope as an optional enhancement; build the core on open Copernicus Sentinel-1 + Sentinel-2 data; resolve access early (RQ8). [Affects: WP1 (Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the field state)]

risk_register.description: Reconciling the differing spatial and temporal resolutions of radar, optical, soil and weather sources may fail or degrade the fusion quality.
risk_register.mitigation: Geospatial/time-series data platform with QC; temporal compositing; explicit resolution handling. [Affects: WP1 (Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the field state)]

risk_register.description: Cloud cover limits Sentinel-2 optical availability, while dense vegetation reduces Sentinel-1 SAR retrieval accuracy - the two sensors' complementary weaknesses.
risk_register.mitigation: Lean on Sentinel-1 SAR through cloud; cloud masking; vegetation-aware retrieval. [Affects: WP1 (Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the field state)]

risk_register.description: Few large-scale efforts collect dense ground truth, so the validation may be under-powered to establish credibility.
risk_register.mitigation: Plan field trials with dense ground truth (RQ4); use a cost-effective sensor network. [Affects: WP3 (Field validation, ground truth and uncertainty calibration)]

risk_register.description: Route B's central assumption - that the chosen homogeneous patch genuinely covaries with the target crop - may not hold, invalidating the proxy.
risk_register.mitigation: Pre-register a covariation test; measure covariation (control stand) rather than assume it (RQ9). [Affects: WP3 (Field validation, ground truth and uncertainty calibration)]

risk_register.description: The framework's headline commitment - honest uncertainty - fails if e.g. 90% prediction intervals do not contain the truth about 90% of the time.
risk_register.mitigation: Build uncertainty-calibration metrics into the validation protocol (RQ5); use uncertainty-aware calibration end to end. [Affects: WP2 (Uncertainty-aware decision engine and demonstrator integration), WP3 (Field validation, ground truth and uncertainty calibration)]

risk_register.description: The rigorous one-step probabilistic fusion route may exceed available modelling expertise, validation data or compute within the fellowship.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep Route B as a credible fallback; stage the build; provision the probabilistic-modelling compute runtime. [Affects: WP1 (Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the field state)]

risk_register.description: Calibrating AquaCrop to a single overconfident parameter set would break the uncertainty chain and produce falsely confident decisions.
risk_register.mitigation: Uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration that retains parameter uncertainty (the fellow-attributed method, doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556). [Affects: WP2 (Uncertainty-aware decision engine and demonstrator integration)]

risk_register.description: Integrating and calibrating heterogeneous sensors (radar, optical, soil, weather) adds complexity that can degrade signal quality.
risk_register.mitigation: QC pipeline; sensor comparison in the validation layer. [Affects: WP1 (Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the field state), WP3 (Field validation, ground truth and uncertainty calibration)]

risk_register.description: Operational frameworks unifying all sensors at scale are scarce, so the demonstrator may not reach a usable pilot within the fellowship.
risk_register.mitigation: Frame the MVP as a standalone research demonstrator; partners assist (feedback, farmer access, testing) rather than own or operate it; set the TRL target explicitly (RQ10). [Affects: WP2 (Uncertainty-aware decision engine and demonstrator integration), WP5 (Dissemination, exploitation, communication and management)]

issues.description: WP2 develops and deploys an AI-based uncertainty-aware decision engine producing water-use-efficiency irrigation recommendations from probabilistic crop model (AquaCrop) outputs calibrated with Bayesian field state posteriors. The system is scoped as a research demonstrator (TRL 3-4); all decisions remain with human operators. Category 8 ethics self-assessment is triggered by the development and use of AI-based systems.
issues.mitigation: System scope is explicitly bounded as a research demonstrator with human-in-the-loop operation; no automated decision-making without human oversight is in scope for this project. Ethical concerns related to AI, human rights, and values will be addressed in the full ethics self-assessment (Part A Section 4 Category 8) at proposal submission. Civil focus is maintained (all activities are advisory/research only).
issues.source_basis: Ethics self-assessment requirement grounded in Tier 1: wp-15-general-annexes p.16 (ethics_self_assessment_required); programme-guide pp.25-28 (ethics appraisal covers proportionality of methods and applicant awareness of ethical and social impacts). Project activity derived from wp_structure.json WP2 title and objectives (uncertainty-aware decision engine; research demonstrator web MVP T2-03). The Tier 3 compliance_profile.json records ethics_review_required: true as a compliance flag derived during call binding; no Tier 2B extracted source path in scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json cites AI ethics review as a topic-specific mandate for this MSCA-PF call beyond the general Tier 1 programme requirement.

issues.description: WP3 field validation on Hungarian tomato farms via VALIDATION_PARTNER (AgroVIR) may involve collection of farm-level data that could be identifiable to individual farmers or farm operators. GDPR compliance is required for any personal data processing.
issues.mitigation: Data collection protocols for WP3 will be designed to anonymise or aggregate farm-level data where feasible. Informed consent procedures will be established for any identifiable data collection. GDPR compliance will be ensured at HOST (ELTE) institutional level, as the sole beneficiary responsible for grant agreement obligations.
issues.source_basis: Ethics self-assessment requirement grounded in Tier 1: programme-guide pp.25-28 (ethics appraisal covers relevant legislation and proportionality of methods); wp-15-general-annexes p.16. Project activity derived from wp_structure.json WP3 objectives (collect non-destructive physiological ground truth on Hungarian tomato farms via AgroVIR) and partners.json VALIDATION_PARTNER role (farmer access, field validation, feedback). The Tier 3 compliance_profile.json records ethics_review_required: true as a compliance flag; no Tier 2B extracted entry specifically mandates personal data ethics assessment for this topic independently of the Tier 1 general programme requirement.

issues.description: All proposed activities across WP1-WP5 are civil in nature: Earth observation data analysis, probabilistic crop modelling, field validation on tomato farms, training and supervision, and dissemination. No excluded activities are involved: no human cloning for reproductive purposes, no intended modification of heritable genetic heritage of human beings, no creation or destruction of human embryos.
issues.mitigation: No mitigation required. Civil focus confirmed across all work packages. Declaration of civil focus compliance is a mandatory checkbox declaration at proposal submission (Part A Declarations).
issues.source_basis: Civil focus constraint grounded in Tier 1: wp-15-general-annexes pp.14-17; ef_he-ria-ia_en.pdf p.7 (civil_focus_constraint: projects must focus exclusively on civil applications). Project scope verified against wp_structure.json (all WPs focus on agricultural remote sensing, probabilistic modelling, precision irrigation advisory, and MSCA-PF training — all civil applications).

ethics_assessment.self_assessment_statement: Ethics self-assessment is required per Tier 1 sources: wp-15-general-annexes p.16 and programme-guide pp.25-28 (ethics_self_assessment_required rule: applicants must complete an ethics self-assessment; projects with ethics issues may undergo ethics review and ethics requirements may become contractual obligations). The Tier 3 compliance_profile.json records ethics_review_required: true as a compliance flag derived during call binding; no Tier 2B extracted source path in scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json independently cites ethics review as a topic-specific mandate for this MSCA-PF call beyond the general Tier 1 programme requirement. Two ethics issue categories are identified: (1) AI-based systems (Category 8): WP2 decision engine development triggers ethics self-assessment obligations; the system is a research demonstrator (TRL 3-4) with human-in-the-loop operation, which is a relevant mitigating factor to be argued in the Part A Section 4 self-assessment. (2) Personal or farm-level data (Category 4): WP3 field validation on tomato farms may involve identifiable farmer data; GDPR-compliant protocols will be designed under HOST responsibility. Gender equality plan compliance: HOST (ELTE) is a higher education establishment in Hungary (EU Member State); the Tier 1 obligation (wp-15-general-annexes pp.18-19; programme-guide pp.16-17) requires such entities to have a gender equality plan at grant signature and during the grant. The Tier 3 compliance_profile.json gender_plan_required: true flag is consistent with and derivable from this Tier 1 criterion applied to HOST entity type — it is not an independent Tier 2B call-specific mandate; no Tier 2B extracted source path cites gender equality plan as a topic-specific mandate for this MSCA-PF call beyond the Tier 1 general obligation. Gender management balance: beneficiaries must promote equal opportunities and aim for gender balance at all levels of personnel assigned to the action, including supervisory and managerial level, per Tier 1 (wp-15-general-annexes p.18). Integration of the gender dimension in research and innovation content follows the Tier 1 default rule that it is mandatory unless the topic explicitly states non-relevance. No Tier 2B exemption source is currently cited in this Phase 6 artifact; Phase 8 drafting must either add the relevant Tier 2B topic-source reference or keep the claim framed as pending call-specific confirmation. Open Science requirements are confirmed in Tier 2B primary sources: SR-05 (scope_requirements.json) / CC-11 (call_constraints.json) mandate training that fosters Open Science culture, knowledge valorisation, and good scientific conduct including research integrity; SR-06 (scope_requirements.json) / CC-12 (call_constraints.json) mandate training for digital collaboration, open access, FAIR data management, citizen science, and societal engagement; SR-07 (scope_requirements.json) / CC-13 (call_constraints.json) mandate a Career Development Plan jointly established by supervisor and researcher, comprising research objectives, training and career needs, transferable skills, teaching, publications planning, and open science participation, submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action (D4-01, due month 3). Dissemination and exploitation plan is required per Tier 1 (wp-15-general-annexes p.4; programme-guide pp.33-39); addressed in WP5 (D5-01 data management plan month 6, D5-02 dissemination and communication activity report month 24). Civil focus confirmed: all proposed activities have an exclusive focus on civil applications per Tier 1 (wp-15-general-annexes pp.14-17).
